text:
santiago: Heads up — we're seeing sustained queue depth growth for mosaic-13b in ap-southeast-1 over the last 20m. Per-model queues show mosaic-13b at ~380 requests in queue, median wait ~2.1s and P99 ~14s.
ops-bot: [ALERT] queue_depth_high: cluster=ap-southeast-1 model=mosaic-13b current=380 threshold=300
maya: ack. Do we know if this is traffic spike or capacity regression? Any recent deploys or scale events?
drew: No deploys on the runtime side in the last hour. CPU/GPU heartbeat looks fine, but I see GPU utilization for that pool creeping to 96% and a backlog of KV cache hot swaps.
cheng: cost note — if we keep falling back to larger batch sizes the token cost will spike. Need to measure e2e cost change before automatic fallback.
santiago: traffic pattern looks like a multi-tenant burst from a single customer IP range, matched by request headers. 60% of queued requests correlate to customer 'acme-markets'.
maya: ok, options:
- tighten admission control for mosaic-13b in ap-southeast-1 (reduce concurrency limit by 15%)
- route new requests for that customer to mosaic-13b-q4 (quantized lower-cost variant) with graceful fallback
- apply short-term soft rate limit per-token for that tenant
drew: I can patch routing to prefer mosaic-13b-q4 for tenant 'acme-markets' and set a canary window of 10m. Command I'll run:
```
redwoodctl route update --region ap-southeast-1 --model mosaic-13b --fallback mosaic-13b-q4 --match tenant=acme-markets --canary 600
```
ira: before you flip anything, share a quick PromQL to show queue growth per-tenant so SRE can monitor. Here's one we use:
```
sum by (tenant) (increase(redwood_queue_depth{region="ap-southeast-1",model="mosaic-13b"}[15m]))
```
katie: I can approve a small temporary capacity bump (hot-spare pool) for 30m if we think this is a burst. That'd add ~8 GPUs to the ap-southeast-1 serving pool.
maya: prefer routing fallback + soft rate limit + canary first. If P99 doesn't improve in 15m we spin the hot spare.
cheng: cost calc quick hit — 8 GPUs @ spot-ish will cost ~ $27/hr for the bump; if it prevents retry storms for a major customer it's likely worth it. But we'll track delta in token spend from fallback.
ops-bot: [ACTION] routing-change-requested by drew for tenant=acme-markets model=mosaic-13b -> mosaic-13b-q4 canary=600
drew: pushed the route canary. Logs:
```
INFO routing: canary 10m added for tenant=acme-markets -> mosaic-13b-q4
INFO routing: 12% of matching traffic routed to fallback (gradual)
```
maya: added a soft per-tenant QPS cap: `tenant.acme-markets.qps=12` for the next 15m.
ira: SRE: please watch these dashboards: Queue depth per-model, request latency per-tenant, fallback-route hit rate. PromQL to watch fallback hit rate:
```
sum(rate(redwood_route_fallbacks_total{region="ap-southeast-1",model="mosaic-13b"}[1m]))
```
oncall-sre: watching. If fallback hit rate > 40% or tail latency doesn't drop in 15m we'll escalate and request hot-spare spin-up.
santiago: after 10m canary: queue depth down to 210, median wait 0.9s, P99 6.2s. Fallback is handling ~34% of matched traffic. Good improvement so far.
maya: nice. keep canary for full 10m then promote if stable. Also submit a follow-up playbook note: why this tenant spikes and whether we should add per-tenant burst SLOs.
cheng: I'll start a short cost diff compute: token units on mosaic-13b-q4 vs mosaic-13b over last 30m and report.
katie: standby on hot-spare; we'll only spin if oncall asks.
santiago: Cool — action items: (1) promote fallback if stable, (2) create post-incident note with tenant pattern, (3) evaluate per-tenant burst policy. I'll open the ticket.
ops-bot: [NOTE] ticket created: INFRA-2918 "ap-southeast-1 mosaic-13b tenant burst handling" assigned to santiago
drew: :thumbsup: closing loop for now. If anyone sees regression ping here or @oncall-sre.
oncall-sre: acknowledged. monitoring until 1865005410.
maya: thanks team. short and surgical fix worked. we'll follow up with policy proposal.
